summary: Reads audio from files on disk or http addresses and always outputs time-sliced audio data. It streams large sources rather than loading the full file into memory, making it a common source for audio-reactive CHOP chains.

key_params.name: file
key_params.note: Audio file path or supported URL.

key_params.name: play
key_params.note: Enable playback when not locked to timeline.

key_params.name: playmode
key_params.note: Locked to Timeline, Specify Index, Sequential, or Timecode Object/CHOP/DAT.

key_params.name: cue
key_params.note: Jump to cue point while held.

key_params.name: cuepulse
key_params.note: Pulse to jump to cue point.

key_params.name: index
key_params.note: Explicit song position for Specify Index mode.

key_params.name: timecodeop
key_params.note: CHOP, DAT, or Timecode object reference for timecode mode.

key_params.name: prereadlength
key_params.note: Buffered audio length for smooth playback.

key_params.name: opentimeout
key_params.note: Milliseconds to wait for the file to open before outputting silence.

key_params.name: autoexportroot
key_params.note: Export root for path-style channel names.

key_concepts: always outputs time sliced audio data
copies http locations to local disk first
common_gotchas: Locked to Timeline disables Play, Reset, Speed, and Index because the timeline directly controls playback position.
A negative Speed is not a reliable reverse-play plan; the official docs state the node cannot play audio backwards well.
Open Timeout can make the CHOP output silence while TouchDesigner keeps retrying the file open, so validate channel energy before mapping to visuals.
Audio File In CHOP always outputs time-sliced audio data; use Record CHOP or Movie File Out TOP when the data must be recorded.
Large disk or http sources stream and keep only a few seconds in memory, so do not assume the entire source is resident.
